questions.prompt: Can you walk on a public sidewalk or sit in a city park with an open beer in Bay St. Louis?
choices: Yes, if you are not driving
No, open containers are not allowed there unless a city exception applies
Yes, but only beer and not wine or liquor
questions.answer: No, open containers are not allowed there unless a city exception applies
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Powers of city concerning regulation of light wines and beer, MCA 1972, § 67-3-65;
               alcoholic beverages, MCA 1972, § 67-1-1 et seq.; intoxicating beverages offenses,
               MCA 1972, §§ 97-31-1 et seq., 99-27-1 et seq.

The purpose of this chapter is to declare the public policy of the city, to prohibit
               any person from carrying, handling or transporting any cereal malt beverage, beer,
               wine or alcoholic or other intoxicating beverage along, upon, or over the public streets,
               alleys, ways, sidewalks, parks, municipally owned or public facilities and parking
               lots within the corporate limits of the city so as to make it possible to extract
               in the places prohibited, the contents or any part thereof from the containers of
               such beverages, since the beverage was originally placed in such container and sealed
               at its place of manufacturing, brewing, distilling, canning or bottling. (Code 1996, § 6-1; Ord. No. 367, § 3, 12-7-1993)

Subject to any exceptions created by ordinance, it shall be unlawful for any person
               to drink or consume any cereal malt beverage, beer, wine or alcoholic or other intoxicating
               beverage of any kind, or to have in his possession, an open container of any cereal
               malt beverage, beer, wine or alcoholic or other intoxicating beverage of any kind
               while in any vehicle, along or upon any public road, street, alley, way, sidewalk,
               park or any city-owned or public facility, or any parking lot intended for use and
               normally used or provided by business for public use, within the city. Any such person
               who violates this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. (Code 1996, § 6-2; Ord. No. 367, § 1, 12-7-1993)

Subject to any exceptions created by ordinance, it shall be unlawful for any…

questions.prompt: Which yard waste can go out with regular garbage in Biloxi?
choices: Hedge clippings and small tree trimmings (no limb over 5 feet long and 4 inches thick)
Any tree limbs if they are stacked neatly at the curb
Concrete, brick, and leftover roofing from a remodel
All building debris if it is in a 30-gallon can
questions.answer: Hedge clippings and small tree trimmings (no limb over 5 feet long and 4 inches thick)
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Beautification commission, § 2-6-1 et seq.; buildings, ch. 5; fire prevention, ch. 7; flood damage prevention, ch. 8; health and sanitation, ch. 11; parks and recreation, ch. 14; streets and sidewalks, ch. 17; subdivision regulations, ch. 18; water and sewers, ch. 22; zoning, ch. 23.

For purposes of this chapter, the word "garbage" is defined as the following: rubbish,
               trash, kitchen waste, restaurant waste, food containers, paper, rags, floor litter,
               sidewalk sweepings, cut or fallen leaves, cut grass, cut weeds, hedge trimmings, small
               tree trimmings provided the tree trimmings do not include limbs in excess of five
               feet in length and four inches in diameter, or other refuse originating on land adjoining
               dwellings or business establishments or on sidewalks, neutral grounds or any public
               property located within the city. (Code 1959, § 9-1-1) Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, § 1-1-2 .

All residences and commercial accounts will have garbage picked up once per week on
               such schedule as may be established by the city. (Code 1959, § 9-1-2; Ord. No. 2402 , § 1, 9-17-19)

(a) No garbage or refuse from human use shall be exposed on the streets or in any yard
               in the city unless such garbage and refuse is kept in a container meeting the specifications
               provided in this section. The container shall be covered at all times when used for
               such purposes. (b) Garbage shall be placed in containers of not more than 30-gallon capacity. The combined
               weight of garbage and container shall not exceed 50 pounds. Containers which weigh
               more than 50 pounds will not be picked up by the garbage collectors. (c) The container shall be a watertight receptacle of a solid and durable grade of metal
               or plastic, or sanitized garbage…

questions.prompt: Drinking or possessing alcohol on most Brandon city streets, sidewalks, and parks is:
choices: Unlawful except in the Downtown Arts and Entertainment District and at the Amphitheater or Municipal Complex with a rental agreement
questions.answer: Unlawful except in the Downtown Arts and Entertainment District and at the Amphitheater or Municipal Complex with a rental agreement
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— The provisions of this chapter which pertain to the sale, consumption of use of alcoholic
               beverages, as that term is defined herein, apply only at such time, if ever, that
               Rankin County votes to come out from under the state's dry law provisions.
               
                 An ordinance adopted Oct. 7, 2013, amended ch. 6 in its entirety to read as herein
               set out. Formerly, ch. 6, §§ 6-1—6-21, pertained to similar subject matter and derived
               from an ordinance adopted Aug. 28, 2013. See the Code Comparative Table for a complete
               derivation. Cross reference— Local privilege taxes, § 74-31 et seq. State Law reference— Alcoholic beverages, MCA 1972, § 67-1-1 et seq.; intoxicating beverage offenses, MCA
               1972, § 97-31-5 et seq.

(a) Except within the Downtown Brandon Arts and Entertainment District as provided in
               this chapter, it shall be unlawful for any persons to have in his possession or to
               consume any alcoholic beverage in or on any public grounds, building, street, sidewalk,

               or current magazine regularly published with not less than four issues per year, and

               notes following amended provisions. The absence of a history note indicates that the
               provision remains unchanged from the original charter. Obvious misspellings have been

               catchlines and citations to state statutes has been used. Additions made for clarity
